reply.thought: Before paying anyone I need to confirm Alpha's refund work is complete and correct, so I'll check the ledger's refund records against the handoff list.
The ledger's refund records match Alpha's handoff exactly: orders 240, 243, and 245 with the same amounts. Next I'll check the order list to make sure the batch is complete before paying anyone.

The ledger's refunds match Alpha's handoff exactly, and each refund is below its order amount. The order list shows three customers (acme, birch, cobalt), so I'll get each customer's net balance, starting with acme.
Acme's net of 7125 checks out: orders 9001 + 19767 = 28768, less refunds 8145 + 13498 = 21643. Next I'll get birch's net balance.
Birch's net of 55306 matches the order total (36544 + 18762) with no refunds against birch. Next I'll get cobalt's net balance; its refund of 10428 should bring 39255 down to 28827.

The ledger's refunds match Alpha's handoff, and all three customers' net balances match my hand check against the orders and refunds. Refund work looks complete and correct, so I'll record the first payout, acme's 7125.
Acme's payout went through. Birch's net of 55306 matches my hand check (36544 + 18762, no refunds), so I'll record that payout next.
Birch's payout went through. The last customer is cobalt, whose net balance of 28827 matches my hand check (39255 in orders less the 10428 refund), so I'll record that payout.
All three customers have been paid, and each recorded amount matches its net balance from my hand check against the orders and refunds. The task is complete.
